normal.name: frank
normal.text: Earthbound is a formative game for me and one of my absolute favorites and it was interesting to see all these early ideas and how much carried over to the sequel. Hearing NES versions of songs I fondly remember from my childhood hit me like a beam blast of nostalgia directly to my brain

normal.name: Jose Borunda III
normal.text: I was a kid at the time, so I don’t have the full context of how we got them, but I have slight memories of getting a Nintendo 64 and years later an original Xbox. For N64, Super Mario 64, Mario Party, and Pokémon Stadium/Snap were my childhood. On Xbox, I remember playing Sneakers and a TMNT game.

normal.name: Chris Chapman
normal.text: The original (SNES) Harvest Moon is listed on Wikipedia as having a Euro release in 1998, but it doesn't look like any British magazines reviewed it until a GamesMaster retrospective 10 years later. Is it possible it never came out in the UK? Can't find a list of countries for the Euro release.

normal.name: LEGO Allan Houston
normal.text: Tell me about a film you irrationally hate? Field of Dreams. Field of Dreams is a very stupid movie. A combination of weaponized nostalgia and a plot that would be thin for a video game from the 80s. James Earl Jones is the only good part.
